document_title: Operational Guidelines for Implementation of PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana (CFA Component to Residential Consumers)
issuing_body: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), Govt. of India
key_rule: The PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana aims to install grid-connected rooftop solar systems in 1 crore residential households across India by FY 2026-27, providing up to 300 units of free electricity every month and reducing carbon footprint.

document_title: Operational Guidelines for Implementation of PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana (CFA Component to Residential Consumers)
issuing_body: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), Govt. of India
key_rule: The scheme applies exclusively to the residential sector including individual households and Group Housing Societies / Residential Welfare Associations (GHS/RWA) for common area facilities across all States and Union Territories in India.

document_title: Operational Guidelines for Implementation of PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana (CFA Component to Residential Consumers)
issuing_body: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), Govt. of India
key_rule: An applicant must be an Indian citizen, possess a residential electricity connection in their name from the local DISCOM (e.g., MSEDCL in Maharashtra), own suitable roof rights or terrace space, and have not previously availed central financial assistance for the same premises.

document_title: Operational Guidelines for Implementation of PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana (CFA Component to Residential Consumers)
issuing_body: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), Govt. of India
key_rule: Central Financial Assistance (CFA) is provided as a fixed subsidy slab: ₹30,000 per kW for systems up to 2 kW capacity, and ₹18,000 per kW for additional capacity between 2 kW and 3 kW. The maximum eligible central subsidy for any general residential system is strictly capped at ₹78,000 (achieved at 3 kW). Systems larger than 3 kW do not receive additional subsidy.

document_title: Operational Guidelines for Implementation of PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana (CFA Component to Residential Consumers)
issuing_body: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), Govt. of India
key_rule: All registrations, application submissions, technical feasibility approvals, vendor selections, metering requests, and subsidy claims must be processed end-to-end through the unified National Portal (pmsuryaghar.gov.in).

document_title: Operational Guidelines for Implementation of PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana (CFA Component to Residential Consumers)
issuing_body: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), Govt. of India
key_rule: The local distribution utility (such as MSEDCL) must issue technical feasibility approval within 15 days of online application submission. If not rejected within this timeframe, deemed technical approval is granted under national guidelines.

document_title: Operational Guidelines for Implementation of PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana (CFA Component to Residential Consumers)
issuing_body: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), Govt. of India
key_rule: Consumers can choose any registered vendor from the National Portal under an open-market model. Vendors must submit performance guarantees, follow MNRE standards, enter into a standard bilateral agreement with the consumer, and provide 5 years of comprehensive maintenance.

document_title: Operational Guidelines for Implementation of PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana (CFA Component to Residential Consumers)
issuing_body: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), Govt. of India
key_rule: A bi-directional net meter must be installed and synchronized with the local grid. Surplus power generated during the day is exported to the DISCOM grid, and net energy accounting is reflected in the monthly electricity bill in accordance with state electricity regulatory commission regulations.

document_title: Operational Guidelines for Implementation of PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana (CFA Component to Residential Consumers)
issuing_body: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), Govt. of India
key_rule: To qualify for CFA, solar modules must strictly comply with Domestic Content Requirement (DCR), utilizing solar cells and modules manufactured in India and listed on the Approved List of Models and Manufacturers (ALMM) issued by MNRE. Inverters must comply with BIS standards.

document_title: Operational Guidelines for Implementation of PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana (CFA Component to Residential Consumers)
issuing_body: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), Govt. of India
key_rule: After plant installation, the vendor submits a work completion report on the portal. DISCOM officials conduct a site inspection, verify net meter integration, and issue a formal Commissioning Certificate which is uploaded directly to the National Portal.

document_title: Operational Guidelines for Implementation of PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana (CFA Component to Residential Consumers)
issuing_body: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), Govt. of India
key_rule: Upon issuance of the commissioning certificate, the consumer submits bank account details and a cancelled cheque on the portal. The central financial assistance (subsidy) is released directly into the consumer's bank account via Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) within 30 days of verification.

document_title: Operational Guidelines for Implementation of PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana (CFA Component to Residential Consumers)
issuing_body: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), Govt. of India
key_rule: Consumers can register complaints regarding vendor performance, installation delays, or DISCOM net metering on the National Portal grievance redressal module. Unresolved vendor disputes lead to blacklisting and forfeiture of the vendor's bank guarantee.

document_title: PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana - National Portal Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
issuing_body: National Portal for Rooftop Solar / MNRE
key_rule: PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana provides free electricity up to 300 units per month through rooftop solar installations. The scheme is open to residential households with individual electricity connections and suitable shadow-free rooftops.

document_title: PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana - National Portal Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
issuing_body: National Portal for Rooftop Solar / MNRE
key_rule: Earlier Phase-II schemes utilized DISCOM-discovered L1 benchmark pricing. Under PM Surya Ghar, prices are market-determined by vendors registered on the National Portal. Typical market turnkey costs range between ₹50,000 to ₹65,000 per kW depending on module technology, inverter specifications, and mounting structure height.

document_title: PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana - National Portal Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
issuing_body: National Portal for Rooftop Solar / MNRE
key_rule: Subsidies are fixed across India: ₹30,000 for 1 kW, ₹60,000 for 2 kW, and ₹78,000 for 3 kW. For systems between 2 kW and 3 kW, subsidy is ₹60,000 plus ₹18,000 per additional kW. Residential systems above 3 kW receive a flat ₹78,000 CFA.

document_title: PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana - National Portal Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
issuing_body: National Portal for Rooftop Solar / MNRE
key_rule: As a rule of thumb, approximately 10 square metres (about 100 to 110 square feet) of shadow-free rooftop area is required for every 1 kW capacity of solar PV installation. For a 3 kW system, approximately 30 sq metres is required.

document_title: PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana - National Portal Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
issuing_body: National Portal for Rooftop Solar / MNRE
key_rule: Solar PV modules must carry a minimum 10-year product warranty and a 25-year performance warranty (generating at least 80% of rated output at year 25). Grid-tied solar inverters must carry a minimum 5-year replacement warranty.

document_title: PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana - National Portal Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
issuing_body: National Portal for Rooftop Solar / MNRE
key_rule: The registered empanelled vendor is obligated to provide 5 years of comprehensive Operation and Maintenance (O&M) including routine system health checks, fault rectifications, and inverter servicing at no extra cost to the consumer.

document_title: PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana - National Portal Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
issuing_body: National Portal for Rooftop Solar / MNRE
topic: FAQ 7: Vendor Selection and Payment Terms
key_rule: Consumers select vendors through the National Portal and execute a standard agreement. The consumer pays the mutually agreed project cost to the vendor, and the central government deposits the eligible subsidy directly into the consumer's bank account after plant commissioning.

document_title: PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana - National Portal Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
issuing_body: National Portal for Rooftop Solar / MNRE
key_rule: The bi-directional net meter records both electricity imported from DISCOM and solar power exported. If exported units exceed imported units in a billing cycle, the net credit is carried forward to subsequent months per state regulatory commission rules.
